extracted.intended_audience: vocational education administrators and faculty; workshop organizers in vocational education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for running a multi-day workshop to teach vocational educators how to prepare grant/project proposals (including course content, participant selection, instructional format, and evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform participants of funding sources and application processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform participants of the existence and proper utilization of funding sources and what is involved in applying for them (e.g., Vocational Education Act and Amendments, foundations, business and industry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The workshop brought in Bureau staff to provide overviews of programs requiring proposals; participants valued the program overviews (Dr. Carroll Curtis). Lack of this information limits participants' ability to identify fundable projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach the essential components/anatomy of a proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform participants of the essential components of a proposal (anatomy of a proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions were scheduled specifically on 'anatomy of a proposal' and 'Proposal Writing.' The report notes participants were informed about the essential parts of a proposal but did not necessarily develop the skills to write them—indicating that explanation alone is insufficient without hands-on practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist participants in writing a quality proposal/prospectus
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist participants in the writing of quality proposals and in developing a prospectus for a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Afternoon individual conferences were devoted to assisting potential projects; of nineteen participants, five developed prospectuses (one excellent, one good, three acceptable). Successful assistance leads to completed prospectuses; failing to provide sufficient time or pre-existing project ideas reduces output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide targeted help on writing objectives, project design and outcomes measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedite proposal writing by providing assistance in the areas of writing objectives, design of project and measurement of outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The session on writing behavioral objectives was singled out as particularly beneficial; five participants reported it would enable better curriculum writing. Workshops should include hands-on practice developing measurable objectives and outcome measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable participants to identify and define the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Help participants identify and define the problem to be addressed by a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the stated objectives was that participants 'identify and define the problem.' The report indicates most participants came without project ideas and thus this objective was only met for a small number of attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce and demonstrate Vocational Education Information Network (VEIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform participants of the Vocational Education Information Network (VEIN) and how to utilize it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miss Erma Keyes' VEIN presentation was well received; many were impressed that information could be obtained easily. Including practical demonstrations of VEIN is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sessions on consortium and cooperative arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover consortium and cooperative arrangements as part of proposal planning (how to structure multi-party projects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule included a session on consortia and cooperative arrangements (Dr. Higgins). This content prepares participants for collaborative funding opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide critiques of proposals and peer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Include critiques of proposals as a scheduled activity to give feedback on prospectuses and drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule lists 'Critiques of proposals' as a planned session. Critiques and peer review are positioned as productive concluding activities to refine proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure the workshop with presentations plus individual conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the workshop with morning presentations for information and afternoon individual conferences for project-specific assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five-day schedule used morning presentations and afternoon individual conferences; this combination allowed information transfer plus individualized drafting help. The report attributes some successes (five prospectuses) to the individual conferencing model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use small group sessions for skill practice (e.g., behavioral objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ small group sessions to practice specific skills like developing behavioral objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small group sessions on developing behavioral objectives were part of the schedule and reinforced the behavioral objectives lecture; participants reported these sessions were useful for curriculum revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite Bureau staff and experts to present program overviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in Bureau staff and other knowledgeable presenters to overview funding programs that require proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned appearances by Bureau staff (Dr. Dittenhefer, Dr. Curtis, Mr. Wayne Grubb) were intended to provide necessary program information; their absence due to flooding reduced workshop effectiveness. Having authoritative presenters is important for legitimacy and content accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select participants based on readiness and existing project ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Select participants on the basis of the idea which they present and upon the basis of their ability within their organization to write a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: participants should be chosen because they have an idea and organizational capacity to pursue a proposal. Many attendees lacked project ideas, which limited the workshop's ability to produce prospectuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertise and obtain bureau-level support to recruit suitable participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the workshop is well advertised and actively promoted by the Bureau of Vocational, Technical and Continuing Education to attract appropriate participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report recommends better advertising and promotion by the Bureau to attract individuals who want to write proposals and come prepared. Administrative support increases participation quality and quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow adequate time and contingency planning for production sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule sufficient time for the most productive drafting sessions and plan contingencies for disruptions (weather, speaker absence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes Thursday and Friday were to be the most productive days but flooding prevented many participants and speakers from attending, reducing output. Workshops should build in contingency plans and ensure critical production days are protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use informal formative evaluation to assess needs and satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the workshop informally through discussions with participants to assess needs and satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation process used informal discussion to assess needs; participants were frank and enthusiastic and expressed satisfaction with certain presentations. Formative evaluation helped identify which sessions were useful (e.g., VEIN, behavioral objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer academic credit as an incentive for deeper engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide college credit options (e.g., independent study credit) for participants to encourage engagement and sustained work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Six of nineteen participants sought and were granted the college credit offered. Credit can motivate participants to invest more effort.
